correctness.rationale: For every horizontal width w and normal height c, the two cap-offset intervals have length w sqrt(1-c²) and centers displaced by 2hc; their overlap and gap lengths are the positive parts of w sqrt(1-c²)-2hc and its negative. Integrating c from 0 to 1 yields g_h(w), h-πw/4+g_h(w), and total h+πw/4. Cauchy perimeter formula normalizes the law. Direct differentiation establishes strictly positive g_h second derivative, proving precisely the constant-width equality class. The small-h limit recovers mean width; all even moments are obtained from the convergent large-h series and the compact Hausdorff moment problem. The supplied two strictly positive-curvature support functions have equimeasurable widths but different exact areas. The packaged checker passes independent angular-offset quadrature and weighted Monte Carlo, and no finite check is taken as proof of the all-convex-body conclusion.

value.rationale: The general right-cylinder family and three natural end-face incidence events are geometrically canonical. The complete probability law yields a parameter-free perimeter statistic, a sharp and nontrivial all-convex-body fixed-perimeter extremal classification including nondisk constant-width minimizers, and a true inverse theorem determining the entire unlabeled width distribution from a scalar height-parameter curve with a sharp explicit failure of body/area recovery. This is a motivated exact structural result, not a routine numeric slice, reparameterization, known table recomputation, or finite-test curiosity.
